title: A Chebyshev-type integral inequality for positive bounded increasing functions, with equality only for constants
author: The Univalent Foundations Program
work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 4.17 at source lines 1905-1912: for a < b and positive bounded increasing functions f, g on the interval, the mean of f g is at least the product of the means, with equality if and only if f or g is constant. The author's proof (source lines 1914-1920) has two parts of different character: the inequality is obtained by constructing two measures of equal mass and showing that one dominates the other through an explicit computation of their cumulative distribution functions, which uses monotonicity of f (line 1916), and then integrating the increasing function g against the dominating measure; the equality analysis is a separate argument that reduces to indicators of intervals [c,b], shows that equality forces c to be an endpoint unless f is constant, and extends the conclusion to positive combinations and then to limits (line 1918). The statement records the inequality and the equality case but neither the comparison of measures nor the reduction to indicators.

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of Lemma 4.17, retained line for line
